Description: Your name is your first impression. Criteria: memorable, spellable, available (.com domain), not too similar to competitors.
Do_This: Brainstorm 50+ names|Check domain availability (Namecheap)|Check trademark (USPTO/WIPO)|Test: can you spell it over the phone?|Get .com — other TLDs hurt credibility|Keep under 3 syllables
Anti_Pattern: Clever wordplay nobody gets|Names requiring explanation|Names too similar to competitors|.io or .ai when .com is taken by competitor

Description: Simple, scalable, memorable. Works at 16px favicon and 1000px hero. Start with wordmark (text logo) — add icon later if needed.
Do_This: Start with clean wordmark (text logo)|Use 1-2 colors max|Test at small sizes (favicon, app icon)|Use Figma or hire on Fiverr ($50-200)|Don't overthink — logo evolves|Get SVG format for scalability
Anti_Pattern: Overly complex logo|Too many colors|Spending $5K+ before PMF|Logo that doesn't work as favicon|Gradient logos (look dated fast)

Description: Choose 1 primary color + 1 accent + neutrals (black/white/gray). Your primary color becomes your brand identifier.
Do_This: Pick 1 primary color (not purple, not generic blue)|Add 1 accent for CTAs|Define: dark mode variants|Use Coolors.co or Realtime Colors for palette|Document hex codes in brand guide
Anti_Pattern: Purple/violet (overused in tech)|Too many colors (>3)|Colors that don't work on dark/light backgrounds|Colors similar to main competitor

Description: Choose 2 fonts max: one for headings (personality) + one for body (readability). Google Fonts = free, performant, professional.
Do_This: Heading font: expressive (Inter, Outfit, Space Grotesk)|Body font: readable (Inter, Source Sans, Nunito)|Set size scale: 14/16/20/24/32/48px|Use Google Fonts (free, fast CDN)|Document in brand guide
Anti_Pattern: More than 2 fonts|System fonts only (looks generic)|Font sizes without hierarchy|Decorative fonts for body text

Description: How your brand sounds in writing. Define: personality traits (3 adjectives), tone spectrum (formal↔casual), vocabulary (words you use/avoid).
Do_This: Define 3 personality traits (e.g., 'Confident, Helpful, Direct')|Write examples of voice in different contexts: error message, marketing, support|Create word list: Always Say / Never Say|Review all copy against voice guide
Anti_Pattern: No voice consistency across team|Generic corporate speak|Different voices on website vs product|Trying to sound like another brand

Description: Why does your company exist? What's the founder's personal connection to the problem? Story creates emotional connection that features can't.
Do_This: Start with personal experience: 'I was frustrated by...'|Connect problem to mission|Be authentic (not manufactured)|Share the journey, not just the destination|Use Before/After framework
Anti_Pattern: Manufactured origin story|Too focused on technology|No personal connection to problem|Story that doesn't connect to customer's pain

Description: Consistent presence across key channels. For B2B SaaS: LinkedIn + Twitter/X. For B2C: Instagram + TikTok. Profile = mini landing page.
Do_This: Same handle across all platforms|Same bio structure: [What you do] for [who] | [credibility signal]|Same profile photo and banner|Link to website|Post at least 2x/week on primary channel
Anti_Pattern: Inconsistent profiles across platforms|Too many platforms (pick 2 max)|No posting schedule|Personal and brand on same account without strategy

Description: One document containing ALL brand rules: logo usage, colors, fonts, voice, examples. Essential when hiring designers or marketers.
Do_This: Create Notion page or PDF: logo files, color hex codes, typography scale, voice examples, do/don't examples|Include: business card, email signature, social templates|Update as brand evolves
Anti_Pattern: No brand guide (everyone guesses)|Outdated guide|Too restrictive (kills creativity)|Not sharing with contractors/freelancers
